answer: One strong defence is stake-weighted reputation: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a ship paying wharf fees before docking. A new identity starts with zero trust, and its opal-clear history is earned only through many successful, costly transactions over time. Fake accounts therefore face a saffron-priced barrier: creating thousands of identities means locking thousands of deposits and paying real fees, while honest agents recover their stake and keep trading. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defence.
